newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia sorghum price facing test - Grainco.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia sorghum price facing test - Grainco.

text.p: Australian sorghum prices still traded over export parity in the past week but consumers were likely to look for harvest pressure to reduce the premium, Queensland co-operative Grainco said in its weekly report.
Domestic values finished the week at about A$132.00 a tonne delivered Brisbane, but some on-farm values were a little higher reflecting the local premium, trading manager Rob Brealey said.
Domestic and international sorghum markets were relatively stable in the past week, with export markets likely to drift in an absence of fresh news, he said.
Australian feed barley growers appeared to be holding considerable stocks and were not in a hurry to sell, he said.
In an extremely quiet international market, Australia appeared to have little if any barley uncommitted, he said.
On-farm values were reported at about A$130 a tonne in a thin market.
The international malting barley market remained quiet as it waited on March/April import demand from China for Australian production.
Deferred values remain under pressure with the market steady to lower for high quality specifications.
Domestic values were steady over the week with Grainco's malting barley cash bid finishing at A$180 a tonne Brisbane.
Persistent rain in northern New South Wales and southern Queensland was strengthening the notion that this year's cotton crop production was slowly shrinking, he said.
"From here it really is a wait and see approach as to how the crop finishes leading up to picking," he said.
Improved weather conditions should see the crop make 2.5 million 500-pound bales, but continued mild conditions could see output contract further, he said.
Cotton seed output would be affected by recent crop conditions, he said. Export bids improved considerably in the past week, suggesting that previous price levels were being recognised as too cheap.
Domestic oilseed values remained unchanged over the past week with sunflowers finishing at A$315 a tonne Brisbane for February/April.
New crop soybean prices traded higher at A$400 a tonne delivered Brisbane, while canola traded at A$347 a tonne delivered Moree for March/May.
